title: Spandex prices rise as BDO & THF surge 15%
summary:
Asia FOB China spandex prices rose only 5.4–6.1 per cent despite BDO and THF costs climbing 17–18 per cent, widening margin pressure for producers.
20D retains the strongest price floor, while 40D faces substitution pressure.
Buyers remain cautious, with controlled inventories and any spandex demand recovery is likely to support THF prices.

title: European Council endorses pacts to deepen EU-Mexico trade ties
summary:
The European Council has adopted two decisions authorising the signing of the EU-Mexico Political, Economic and Cooperation Strategic Partnership Agreement and of the interim Trade Agreement between the EU and Mexico.
Together, these aim at strengthening political dialogue, deepening cooperation and boosting sustainable trade and investment.
These will benefit over 45,000 EU companies exporting to Mexico.

title: PTA prices inch up from month-low as oil jumps
summary:
PTA spot prices rebounded 2.3 per cent to $875 per MT on May 11 after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s peace proposal, reviving crude-linked risk premiums.
Earlier ceasefire hopes had dragged prices to $855 per MT.
Buyers remain cautious, while Indian Oil Corporation Limited’s Paradip PTA plant could reshape India’s supply balance in H2 2026.

title: Global cotton production, stocks to fall; consumption to rise: WASDE
summary:
United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) has forecast lower global cotton production and ending stocks, alongside higher consumption for 2026/27, indicating tighter global supplies.
The WASDE report projects world output at 116 million bales and consumption at a six-year high of 121.7 million bales, supported by higher synthetic fibre costs and stronger cotton demand.

title: ICE cotton retreats from multi-month highs on dollar pressure
summary:
ICE cotton futures ended mixed after Monday’s sharp rally, as a stronger US dollar triggered profit-booking despite bullish USDA supply-demand estimates.
July 2026 cotton settled 1.65 per cent lower at 86.32 cents/lb, though volumes stayed exceptionally high.
Markets remained supported by tight supply expectations, while traders monitored US inflation, Fed outlook and US–China tariff uncertainty.

title: GFS 2026: Kering, H&M on putting sustainability back on the CFO agenda
summary:
Global Fashion Summit (GFS) 2026 highlighted the CFO’s growing role in embedding sustainability into fashion’s financial decision-making.
As earnings calls focus more on margins, AI and geopolitics, sustainability mentions have declined by about one-third since 2022.
The BCG-GFA report says CFOs must help prioritise, fund and measure circularity, EPR readiness and long-term resilience.

title: Australia’s business conditions weaken as costs surge in April: Survey
summary:
Australia’s business conditions weakened in April 2026 as NAB’s survey showed sharply rising cost pressures after the Middle East conflict. 
Purchase costs grew 4.5 per cent in quarterly terms, far outpacing product prices and squeezing margins, especially in manufacturing. 
Business conditions fell to plus 3, confidence stayed deeply negative, and forward orders, capex, and employment all softened.

title: Tariff refund mirage: Why apparel’s sourcing shock persists
summary:
US apparel importers may see International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) tariff refunds, but Section 122 relief is not automatic.
The May ruling weakens the 10 per cent surcharge, yet benefits are limited to named plaintiffs.
Importers must act entry by entry, track liquidation timelines, preserve claims, and model July tariff scenarios carefully.

title: India captures Europe's apparel sourcing pivot
summary:
India has overtaken peers as Europe’s fastest-growing apparel supplier; EU-27 imports hit a record $6.96 billion in 2025, up 14.3 per cent YoY. 
Q1 surged 22.3 per cent, the strongest quarter in 4 years; home textiles climbed 18.6 per cent to $1.60 billion.
The zero-duty India-EU FTA wipes a 12 per cent tariff gap as Bangladesh logs 113 factory closures and Turkiye slides 11.3 per cent.

title: Canada, Vietnam seek broader trade cooperation
summary:
Canada and Vietnam have agreed to further strengthen economic and trade ties as well as supply chain connectivity amid growing global uncertainties. 
The issue was discussed at a meeting between Minister of Industry and Trade Le Manh Hung and Canadian ambassador to Vietnam Jim Nickel, who highlighted Vietnam’s growing role in global supply chains. 
The two sides discussed talks on the ASEAN-Canada FTA.

title: Bangladesh’s BGMEA, OS Hub sign MoU to strengthen apparel transparency
summary:
Bangladesh trade body BGMEA and US-based Open Supply Hub have signed an MoU to strengthen apparel sector transparency and digitally presenting factory information on the global supply chain platform.
The two sides will create an integrated digital database platform that will enable buyers to directly access information on the location, product categories and special capabilities of garment units.

title: RMG trade bodies seek policy support from Bangladesh PM
summary:
Representatives of two top Bangladesh garment trade bodies recently met PM Tarique Rahman and urged him to ensure uninterrupted power and energy supply, quick release of export receipts from banks, reopening of closed factories and easing of customs regulations.
BKMEA raised concerns about misuse of the bond facility and urged action against violators of bond licences.

title: US’ Under Armour eyes gross margin improvement in FY27
summary:
For FY27, Under Armour expects slight revenue decline and margin improvement. 
The company’s FY26 revenue fell 4 per cent to $5 billion, led by weaker North America sales, lower wholesale revenue, and a sharp footwear decline. 
Gross margin narrowed due to tariffs and cost pressures. 
In Q4, revenue slipped 1 per cent as North America weakened, though international and DTC sales grew.

title: Israel’s Delta Galil posts record Q1 sales on broad-based growth
summary:
Delta Galil Industries has reported record Q1 2026 sales of $573 million, up 15 per cent YoY, with gross profit rising 18 per cent to $238.8 million. 
The gross margin improved to 41.7 per cent, supported by factory efficiency and favourable exchange rates. 
EBIT also reached a Q1 record, while the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance.

title: Bangladesh BGMEA, Germany’s GIZ sign MoU for green RMG transformation
summary:
Bangladesh trade body BGMEA and Germany’s GIZ recently signed an MoU to strengthen sustainability, energy efficiency and circularity in Bangladesh’s RMG industry. 
The MoU will remain effective from May 2026 to February 2028. 
The cooperation is designed to align industrial growth with international sustainability benchmarks and climate commitments. 
A major focus is energy transition of the sector.

title: Bangladesh passed China but missed the US sourcing shift
summary:
Bangladesh has overtaken China in US apparel supplies, but mainly because China’s shipments collapsed faster.
OTEXA data show Bangladesh’s US exports fell 8.38 per cent, while Vietnam and Cambodia gained share.
TexPro indicates Bangladesh remains woven-heavy, limiting its ability to capture China’s MMF-led shift.
Future gains depend on fibre diversification, speed and value-added capability.

title: Bangladesh RMG sector to adopt blockchain-based transparency & DPP
summary:
Bangladesh’s readymade garment (RMG) sector is set to adopt blockchain-based transparency and Digital Product Passport (DPP) systems ahead of the European Union’s 2027 regulations. 
BGMEA and Dutch traceability platform AWARE signed an MoU to enable end-to-end traceability of fibres, yarns, and garments through blockchain-backed digital records, helping exporters strengthen compliance.

title: India’s KKCL posts strong FY26 growth under Vision 2028
summary:
Kewal Kiran Clothing Limited (KKCL) has reported 20.9 per cent YoY revenue growth to ₹1,212.8 crore (~$121.28 million) in FY26. 
EBITDA rose 24.8 per cent to ₹237.9 crore (~$23.79 million), while PAT increased 2.1 per cent to ₹152.3 crore (~$15.23 million). 
The company credited Vision 2028 execution, strong distribution growth, and the Kraus Casuals acquisition for the performance.

title: US’ Kontoor Brands' posts strong Q1, plans Lee divestiture
summary:
Kontoor Brands has posted stronger-than-expected Q1 FY26 results, driven by growth in Wrangler and Helly Hansen, and raised its full-year outlook. 
Total revenue reached $808 million, while continuing operations generated $613 million. 
The company plans to divest Lee, now treated as a discontinued operation. 
Adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $6.6-6.7 for FY26.

summary:

Both sides will work to introduce decarbonisation methodologies to BGMEA members, and support the sector in exploring advanced, energy-efficient industrial machinery.
